triples.subject: Father Zossima
triples.quote: As the deceased was a priest and monk of the strictest rule, the Gospel, not the Psalter, had to be read over his body by monks in holy orders.

triples.subject: Father Païssy
triples.quote: “Such immediate expectation of something extraordinary,” he said, “shows a levity, possible to worldly people but unseemly in us.”

triples.subject: Father Iosif
triples.quote: The reading was begun by Father Iosif immediately after the requiem service.

triples.subject: Job
triples.quote: One such, whose memory was particularly cherished, was an old monk, Job, who had died seventy years before at the age of a hundred and five.

triples.subject: Father Varsonofy
triples.quote: Another memory cherished in the monastery was that of the famous Father Varsonofy, who was only recently dead and had preceded Father Zossima in the eldership.

triples.subject: Rakitin

triples.subject: Decomposition of Father Zossima's body

triples.subject: Father Ferapont
triples.quote: As every one was aware, Father Ferapont particularly disliked Father Zossima.

triples.subject: Father Païssy
triples.quote: “What have you come for, worthy Father? Why do you offend against good order? Why do you disturb the peace of the flock?” he said at last, looking sternly at him.

triples.subject: Father Ferapont
triples.quote: I have mentioned already that he rarely left his wooden cell by the apiary.

triples.subject: Father Ferapont
triples.quote: As soon as he began waving his arms, the cruel irons he wore under his gown could be heard clanking.

triples.subject: Father Païssy
triples.quote: Father Païssy, with a stern face, continued firmly and distinctly reading aloud the Gospel, apparently not noticing what was taking place around him

triples.subject: Father Ferapont
triples.quote: “What have I come for? You ask why? What is your faith?” shouted Father Ferapont crazily.

triples.subject: Father Ferapont
triples.quote: The dead man, your saint,” he turned to the crowd, pointing with his finger to the coffin, “did not believe in devils.
